system_metadata.author: Dan Olsen
system_metadata.grounding_source: The Lean Product Playbook: How to Innovate with Minimum Viable Products and Rapid Customer Feedback (2015)

space_pen_mirage.analogy: Paul Fisher spending $1 million inventing the Space Pen while Russian astronauts used pencils.
space_pen_mirage.risk: Jumping into solution space before defining the core problem.
space_pen_mirage.action: Separate What (problem space) from How (solution space) before design begins.

follow_me_home.analogy: Intuit employees following Quicken buyers home to watch install and first use.
follow_me_home.action: Prioritize direct behavioral observation over polite survey comments.

oprah_versus_spock.action: Use Oprah to validate product-market fit on paper; use Spock to optimize metrics after launch.

silver_bullet_metric.analogy: Friendster's address-book importer doubling invites per sender in one week.
silver_bullet_metric.action: Find low-effort, high-upside levers with compound growth.

local_maximum_hill.analogy: Optimizing a landing page to a local peak while missing a global maximum that needs a pivot.
local_maximum_hill.action: When iterative tests flatten, zoom out to target customer or value proposition.

olsen_hierarchy_of_web_needs.5_ux_design: How easy and enjoyable the product is to use.
olsen_hierarchy_of_web_needs.4_feature_set: Functionality that meets a customer need.
olsen_hierarchy_of_web_needs.3_absence_of_bugs: Quality — does it work as supposed to?

must_haves.definition: Table stakes; absence causes extreme dissatisfaction.

performance_features.definition: More is better; satisfaction scales with fulfillment.
performance_features.example: Fuel efficiency or page load speed.

delighters.definition: Unexpected wow; absence does not dissatisfy.

kano_model_categories.migration_rule: Yesterday's delighters become today's performance features and tomorrow's must-haves.

I.definition: Independent. Overlap-free and implementable in any order.
I.check: Needs the backlog and what ships before this story; the sentence alone cannot give a pass.

N.definition: Negotiable. Not an explicit contract, so it stays open to discussion.
N.check: Read the want clause and swap the implementation; if the sentence collapses, N fails.

V.definition: Valuable. Delivers a clear benefit to the end user.
V.check: Read the so-that clause; if the benefit lands on the team rather than the actor, V fails.

E.definition: Estimable. Scope can be reasonably estimated by developers.
E.check: Needs the estimating team and what it has built before; the sentence alone cannot give a pass.

S.definition: Small. Short in scope, and large epics must be broken down.
S.check: Needs the sprint length and team capacity; the sentence alone cannot give a pass.

T.definition: Testable. Has clear acceptance criteria that confirm completion.
T.check: Read the test hook; if no observation would settle it either way, T fails.

sean_ellis_pmf.question: How would you feel if you could no longer use [product]?

adoption_lifecycle.action: Name one segment as a hypothesis until purchase or adoption evidence confirms it; do not treat polite interest as proof of position.

rungs: Is actively searching for a solution
Has cobbled together a makeshift workaround
Has budget to pay for a solution
earlyvangelist_ladder.action: Treat each rung as yes, no, or unknown; a sympathetic listener who fails the money or workaround rungs is not an earlyvangelist buyer yet.

roi_prioritization_matrix.return_axis: Low, medium, or high value created for the customer
roi_prioritization_matrix.effort_axis: Low, medium, or high investment in developer-weeks or story points
roi_prioritization_matrix.bucket_1: High return, low effort — top priority quick wins for v1
roi_prioritization_matrix.bucket_2_3: High return medium effort or medium return low effort — secondary MVP candidates
roi_prioritization_matrix.bucket_8_9: Low return, high effort — cut or defer; active waste
roi_prioritization_matrix.action: Map each atomic feature chunk to a bucket, then draw the v1 cut versus v1.1 and v1.2 roadmap from that placement.

aarrr_framework.action: List the metrics you would watch at each stage before picking a single optimization target.

mtmm_retention_first.definition: Metric That Matters Most — one metric that gets all engineering and design effort for a cycle
mtmm_retention_first.retention_priority: Optimize retention (the leak in the bucket) before spending on acquisition if cohort curves decay to zero
mtmm_retention_first.action: Pick one MTMM based on upside and diminishing returns; brainstorm features to move only that metric until the next cycle.
